description: Governed freshness windows for every output published under /.well-known/ (REQ-PUB-2, REQ-GOV-1). The single source for the maximum age of each artifact: scripts/build-trust-center.py, scripts/check-evidence-freshness.py and the evidence SLA watchdog (infrastructure/watchdog.tf and infrastructure/watchdog/) all read it, and each fails closed if it is missing or invalid. Signatures (.bundle), schemas and the human-readable .md renderings are published with the artifact they accompany and are covered through it.
rationale: Nightly evidence (the VDR, its trend and attestation) must be under 24 hours old, the reporting policy. The runtime signal and the nightly's status beacon get 26 hours: one daily (or twice-daily) run plus one late run. Artifacts regenerated only on a deploy, which is human-initiated and human-approved, get 30 days, the monthly continuous-monitoring cadence: older than that, the inventory has not been re-derived from live state within a reporting month. The operator-run independent corroboration gets the same 30 days.

artifacts.note: Provenance attestation; a DSSE envelope with no timestamp of its own, so the object's last-modified time is used.
CR26 Vulnerability Detail Report (VER-RPT-VDT), rebuilt from every VDR report.
CR26 Accepted Vulnerability Info (VER-RPT-AVI), rebuilt from every VDR report.
CR26 historical vulnerability activity (VER-TFR-MRH; Class C SHOULD update at least every 14 days), rebuilt from every VDR report.
Monthly vulnerability detection and response activity report, month to date (VER-TFR-MHR, VER-RPT-HLO, VER-RPT-PER), rebuilt from every VDR report.

Non-machine verification and validation (VDR-TFR-NMV): machine checks of every resource in data/non-machine-resources.json (scripts/_nonmachine.py), run by the deploy (enforced) and the evidence nightly (twice a day). verifiedAt is the run's time when every check passes and the epoch when any fails, so a failing check turns this window red at once; 26 hours means nightly runs have been missed. No verification is manual.
The nightly's status beacon. Unsigned and not evidence; listed because the watchdog pages on its age. The nightly runs twice a day, so 26 hours means runs have been missed.

The incident log (IEC-CSO-EFR) and, through it, every incident report it lists with its sha256. Rebuilt by .github/workflows/incident-reports.yml on every change to data/incidents.json and twice a day, and by every deploy. The report deadlines themselves are hours, so the watchdog also pages on each listed report past its deadline (IncidentReportsOverdue).

SIMULATION: the delivery log of every incident report to a simulated FedRAMP and agency recipient; nothing is sent. Rebuilt with the incident log by every deploy and by .github/workflows/incident-reports.yml.
Signed in-band (provenance.attestation) by the runtime Lambda, which runs daily; 26 hours tolerates one late run.
Rebuilt on every deploy and daily by package-maintenance.yml at the deployed commit; 14 days is CPO-CSX-CPM's Class C maximum, so the watchdog pages before the package falls out of date.
Rebuilt on every deploy and daily by package-maintenance.yml at the deployed commit; 14 days is CPO-CSX-CPM's Class C maximum, so the watchdog pages before the package falls out of date.
Rebuilt on every deploy and daily by package-maintenance.yml at the deployed commit; 14 days is CPO-CSX-CPM's Class C maximum, so the watchdog pages before the package falls out of date.

Index of the issued Ongoing Certification Reports and their snapshots (CCM-OCR-AVL, CDS-CSO-HAD). Only package-maintenance.yml writes it, on its daily schedule and when every deploy calls it (job package-maintainer); cadence 'nightly', the scheduled unattended run, because the maintainer is what writes it. The issues (ocr-issue-<date>.*) and snapshots (snapshot-<date>.json, snapshots/<date>/) it lists are immutable by design, so they carry no freshness window: the index records each one's sha256.

The automated audit-log review (KSI-MLA-RVL, KSI-CMT-RVP; DEC-195): CloudTrail write events and GitHub's record of main since the previous review, judged by rule, with a planted simulated intruder caught every run (scripts/audit-log-review.py). Written by evidence-nightly.yml, its only writer, twice a day; 26 hours means nightly runs have been missed.

Index of the monthly recovery exercises (KSI-RPL-TRC; DEC-195), rewritten on every evidence nightly run (scripts/hold-recovery-exercise.py), its only writer. Each exercise (vdr-recovery-exercise-<date>.*) is immutable and listed with its sha256, so it carries no window; the nightly and the deploy fail from the day after a due date with none published (scripts/check-scheduled-review.py).

Index of the Annual Security Reviews (KSI-PIY-RIS/RES, KSI-SVC-EIS, KSI-INR-RPI; DEC-195) and the rules-of-behavior acknowledgements (PL-4), rewritten daily by package-maintenance.yml (its only writer, so cadence 'nightly', the scheduled unattended run), with the same 14-day window as the package it maintains. Each review (security-review-<date>.*) is immutable and listed with its sha256. The deploy and the evidence nightly fail from the day after a due date with no review in it (scripts/check-scheduled-review.py).

Index of the Quarterly Reviews held with simulated attendees (CCM-QTR-MTG, CCM-QTR-RTR; DEC-194), rewritten daily by package-maintenance.yml (its only writer, so cadence 'nightly', the scheduled unattended run) from the first review date on. The reviews (quarterly-review-<date>.*) it lists are immutable by design, so they carry no freshness window: the index records each one's sha256. The deploy and the evidence nightly fail when a review date has passed with no review in it (scripts/check-quarterly-review.py).
Quarterly Review calendar file (CCM-QTR-REG), from the CCM calendar; written by the deploy and daily by package-maintenance.yml. Not signed: the same dates are in the signed CPO and OCR.
Index of FedRAMP Certification Reports published unmodified (CDS-CSO-FRC). FedRAMP is simulated: the one report is a stand-in.
Log of the simulated submission of the certification package to FedRAMP on each deploy (FRC-CSO-PKG). Nothing is sent.
Run by the operator (tools/boundary-map/corroborate.py), committed, and signed and published by the deploy.
The conformance suite's results for the method profile (REQ-GOV-2), run, signed and published by the deploy.
Monthly aggregate counts of access to the certification data (CDS-TRC-ACL), rebuilt from the CloudFront access records on every deploy.
How to verify and validate each FedRAMP rule and KSI, generated from the rule records on every deploy (IVV-CSO-STE, IVV-CSO-DUS); the simulated assessor runs its checks.
The simulated assessor's signed result set (not a FedRAMP Recognized assessment), produced on every deploy and signed by the simulated-assessor.yml workflow identity, not the deploy's.
Per rule record, whether each test it cites passed in the build that published it (FRC-CSX-VVR).
The agency access procedure run on every deploy against fictional agencies, including the 5-business-day denial clock (CDS-TRC-AAI, CDS-UTC-AAD).
The signed index of all certification data with media types, signatures and human-readable forms (CDS-TRC-PAC).
SIMULATION: the FedRAMP Security Inbox is simulated for this proof of concept; this is the deploy's run of the inbox logic over synthetic messages.
Significant Change Notifications index (SCN-CSO-HIS/HRM/NOM), rebuilt every deploy from docs/scn/scn-register.csv; never pruned.
Atom feed of the SCN notices (SCN-CSO-NOM); its <updated> is the last notice's date, so the object's last-modified time is used.
Append-only significant-change evaluation log (SCN-CSO-MAR), one entry per change merged to main.
